changes: Ribbon questions show the ribbon and ask which it is; insignia questions sometimes show the insignia instead of describing it.
Added what each color of the American flag stands for. The first amphibious landing is now a standard question.

Rank questions now describe an insignia and ask which rank wears it, for cadet, Marine Corps and Navy ranks. Rank order and pay grade questions are no longer asked; they stay in the rank charts and the order game.
Six plain Marine Corps history questions added, such as the first woman to enlist in the Marine Corps.
Marine Corps and Navy ranks added: enlisted and officer ranks in order from the top, plus the pay grade of each rank.
Leadership principles and traits are no longer asked by number, since they have no set order. Use the KKBEMETSKIDS and JJDIDTIEBUCKLE memory aids to learn them.
Removed the question on where general badges are worn: cadets wear marksmanship badges only, and those questions stay.
Chain of command: the people who hold each office are listed first, before the order of the chain.
Memory aids added: JJDIDTIEBUCKLE for the 14 leadership traits and KKBEMETSKIDS for the 11 leadership principles.
Marine Corps: every fact checked again. Drill now follows the current drill manual, MCO 5060.20 (2019): quick time is 112 to 120 steps a minute, close and normal interval are defined by arm position.

Marine Corps: leadership principle 6 reads "Ensure"; the Secretary of Defense (also styled Secretary of War) is named; physical fitness test scores and three grooming rules are marked unconfirmed until a current source is found; items cadets are not asked were removed.
New study content for Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force and Coast Guard JROTC, each from that program's own publications. Some modules are not available yet for some branches.
First amphibious landing: the answer now names New Providence Island and Nassau.
Belt: one question, answered 2 to 4 inches. The separate cloth belt question is removed; its measurement is kept as a note.
Removed two items cadets are not asked: what the rank structure is modeled on, and what decides which ranks a unit uses.
First Marine Corps content set: 291 facts across Ranks, Ribbons, Chain of Command, Uniform, Drill, Knowledge and Regulations, taken from the Marine Corps JROTC Cadet Handbook.
Office holders checked on 12 Nov 2026: President, Vice President, Acting Secretary of the Navy, Commandant, Assistant Commandant, Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps, Director of MCJROTC.
Not yet verified, shown without a name: Secretary of Defense, Region Director.

facts.text: A cadet may be disenrolled for academic failure, ineptitude or poor attitude.

facts.text: A cadet who fails to maintain the minimum GPA set by the SMI and approved by the principal is placed on probation during the next semester.
facts.q: What happens when a cadet falls below the minimum GPA?

facts.text: A cadet on academic probation who does not raise the GPA during the next semester is suspended from MCJROTC and must turn in all uniforms.
facts.q: What happens if a cadet on academic probation does not raise the GPA?
facts.a: Suspension from MCJROTC and turn-in of all uniforms

facts.text: The MCJROTC curriculum is called Leadership Education.
facts.q: What is the MCJROTC curriculum called?

facts.text: Leadership Education has five categories: Leadership; Citizenship; Personal Growth and Responsibility; Public Service and Career Exploration; and General Military Subjects.
facts.q: What are the five categories of Leadership Education?

facts.text: LE-II introduces civilian marksmanship training and land navigation with map and compass.

facts.text: In LE-III cadets take positions of increased authority, and receive detailed instruction on personal finances.

facts.text: LE-IV cadets conduct formations and inspections and supervise training of younger cadets.

facts.text: Part of the MCJROTC grade is leadership performance: carrying out cadet duties and taking part in citizenship and other MCJROTC activities.

facts.text: Cadets are expected to attend all JROTC functions, and to tell the instructors in advance when they cannot.
